text_blocks.snippet: Federal prosecutors, local sheriff's offices, and consumer protection groups have issued warnings about active scams targeting residents across Central Illinois.
snippet_highlighted_words: active scams targeting residents across Central Illinois

list.snippet: U.S. Attorney & Law Enforcement Impersonation: Scammers spoof phone numbers and pose as federal prosecutors or staff from the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of Illinois , making aggressive threats and demanding immediate money or personal information. (Note: Federal prosecutors never request money or financial details over the phone).

AI Voice-Cloning & Romance Scams: Scammers are increasingly using artificial intelligence and voice-cloning technology to mimic family members or trusted entities, alongside romance schemes that build fake online relationships to steal thousands of dollars.

DMV / Traffic Violation / Toll Text Scams: Fraudulent texts from fake "Secretary of State" or toll authorities claim you owe money for traffic violations or tolls and threaten to suspend your vehicle registration. The Illinois Secretary of State’s Office only texts for appointment reminders—never for fees, fines, or personal account info.

Utility & Discount Impersonation: Voicemails and calls spoofing companies like Comcast/Xfinity offer fake bill discounts (e.g., 50% off) to trick people into surrendering account access and financial data.
Driveway Paving & Home Improvement Scams: Traveling contractors or door-to-door crews offer cheap paving or repair services using substandard materials and high-pressure tactics.
Hang up and verify: If a caller claims to be from a government agency, bank, or utility, hang up and call the organization's official, published phone number directly.
Establish a family codeword: Set up a secret verbal code with family members to verify identities during unexpected emergency or "bail" calls.
Never pay via gift cards, wire transfer, or crypto: Legitimate government agencies and businesses will never demand payment through untraceable methods.
Check local alerts: Follow resources like the Peoria County Sheriff's Office or financial institutions like Central Bank Illinois for local fraud updates.
Federal Trade Commission (FTC): Report online at reportfraud.ftc.gov
Local Law Enforcement: Contact your county sheriff’s office or local police dispatch (such as Bloomington Police dispatch at 309-820-8888 for local reports).

text_blocks.snippet: If you received a specific text, call, or email, tell me what they claimed so I can let you know if it matches a known active scam.
